summary: PM announced that from 1 Jan 2027 automotive plastic parts that can be made locally (by GPI Tissemsilt) will no longer be imported.
implication: Creates captive local demand but it is pre-assigned to a state molder (GPI). Small private molder should not fight GPI head-on; look for Tier-2 parts GPI does not cover.

summary: GPI (Holding ACS) inaugurated in Khemisti, Tissemsilt: 251,000 parts/yr for ~200,000 vehicles; 40% integration rising to 70%; scope also lists appliances, fridges, ACs, cable-industry components, medical, packaging, household goods, road signs; 300 direct jobs.
implication: A state competitor now explicitly targets appliance and cable-industry parts too, so check GPI's catalogue before quoting Condor/ENICAB-type buyers.

summary: PM Sifi Ghrieb launched the GPI project; Horizons frames it as acceleration of auto industry relaunch.
implication: Policy momentum for local plastics in vehicles; also a signal that the state prefers public champions.

summary: Minister Rekkache stressed developing industrial subcontracting to raise local integration rates.
implication: Integration-rate pressure on OEMs is the main lever to open purchasing doors.

summary: ENIEM signed Turkish (heaters, >60% integration by June 2025) and Chinese (ACs, CKD order for 30,000 units) partnerships; target 80% integration in 2025.
implication: Integration targets imply need for local plastic sub-parts (heater housings, knobs, AC parts).

summary: ENIEM AC production start postponed from Aug to Dec 2024 because of administrative and logistics delays (Red Sea).
implication: Import-lead-time pain at an OEM; local short-lead supply has value.

summary: ENIEM stopped production (technical stop, ~2020-21; 1,700 staff sent on leave) due to raw-material stockouts in all workshops and lack of bank credit for supplies; full stop in 2023, wages unpaid Oct 2023–Jan 2024; debt ~5 bn DA.
implication: Real pain but HIGH payment risk – require advance/cash terms with ENIEM.

summary: Minister Ali Aoun affirmed commitment to ENIEM revival during Tizi Ouzou visit.
implication: Possible restart orders; monitor.

summary: Géant Electronics adds two units (ACs, fridges) in BBA next to six existing; fridge integration 70%; exports Mauritania/Tunisia, Senegal planned.
implication: BBA appliance cluster growing; target purchasing for small parts.

summary: Condor–Hisense AC complex in BBA: 2M units/yr, 80% export, USD 200M, start expected early 2026.
implication: Very large volumes of AC sub-parts; likely captive/Chinese supply chain, but secondary supplier slots possible.

summary: Samha (Guedjel, Sétif) ~4,000 staff, 5M units/yr capacity; AC integration target only 30–40%.
implication: Low integration = many imported plastic parts; potential localisation buyer.

summary: Samsung Electronics Algeria planned a new AC unit in Sétif in 2024 with partner Sinova (CKD/SKD).
implication: Sétif HVAC assembly cluster = target geography.

summary: Condor integration 45–100% by line; fridge '100% algérien' incl. compressor.
implication: Condor molds in-house; sell overflow/specialty parts only.

summary: Brandt (Cevital) makes most of its own plastic and metal parts and PCBs.
implication: Large OEMs are weak targets for standard parts.

summary: Raylan (Annaba) described as import-export of Hitachi/Electrolux appliances.
implication: Not a component buyer today.

summary: Izdihar PVC (Tiaret, Zaaroura) inaugurated: 117,000 units/yr, 712 MDA, claimed 85% integration; a metallic-hardware (quincaillerie) plant opened the same day.
implication: New PVC window makers need packers, end caps, drainage caps; a local metal-hardware maker may want plastic sub-parts.

summary: Oxxo (Cevital, Aïn Taghrout BBA): 2.1M windows/yr, 23 KraussMaffei extruders, 19 profile lines, ~3,000 staff.
implication: Largest single joinery buyer; probably system hardware from abroad – test for glazing packers/caps.

summary: When 851 products were suspended from import, finished aluminium joinery was removed from the list at the last minute while PVC joinery stayed banned; operators questioned the asymmetry.
implication: Import policy for joinery shifts; local PVC joinery has been protected – supports local accessory demand.

summary: Report that raw materials for aluminium joinery are taxed more heavily than imported finished products.
implication: Tariff inversion hurts local joiners; check current duty on accessories vs finished windows.

summary: Leader Aluminium (Hammedi, Boumerdès) Ouedkniss store lists accessories (brands cited Dubral, Alupha), PVC profiles, EPDM joints; visible prices include 695 DA and 5,950 DA (items not identifiable).
implication: Accessory distributors are active on Ouedkniss; field visit needed to capture unit prices and origin.

summary: Master Italy (Italian accessory maker since 1986) exhibited at Batimatec; distributes in North Africa for 20+ years.
implication: Branded imported systems are the incumbent; local supplier must compete on generic/consumable parts.

summary: Turkish extrusion-line maker Maxtruder promoted participation at Batimatec 2026 (3–7 May).
implication: Equipment vendors see PVC profile investment in Algeria; more profile makers = more accessory buyers.

summary: OTA (Optimum Télécom Algérie) tender for wood/metal/aluminium joinery materials and glazing.
implication: Corporate tenders sustain installer demand.

summary: Procamp advertises aluminium joiner jobs in energy/mining category on Emploitic.
implication: In-house joinery shops at contractors are additional accessory buyers.

summary: Holcim El-Djazaïr launches concrete (béton) activity.
implication: More structured concrete supply chain; rebar spacers sold to contractors not to Holcim itself.

summary: Cosider Canalisations added a precast boundary-wall line and double-T slab moulds.
implication: Precast plants are direct buyers of spacers and cast-in plastic inserts.

summary: Algerian e-shop retail: vertical spacer 150 pcs 840 DA (~5.6 DA/pc); round 30/8-14 1,000 pcs 13,600 DA; horizontal 40-8/24 600 pcs 13,500 DA (~22.5 DA/pc).
implication: Retail price is several times the resin cost; bulky item = freight-protected; good GO candidate (see prior note cost_inputs_market_prices.md for exact URLs).

summary: Pack of 100 OZTURK (Turkish) 7x200 cable ties 450 DZD retail.
implication: Turkish imports dominate shelf; commodity, low-weight = weak local edge.

summary: Local brand HAOUAS boxes sold next to Spanish FAMATEL on Algerian e-shops.
implication: Electrical boxes already locally molded – compete only with differentiation.

summary: Aster (Italy) and Caudal (Spain) list Algeria among trading markets.
implication: Imported branded driplines/fittings are the incumbent; local fittings must match on fit and price.

summary: An Algiers-based producer offers drip tape (1,500 m and 3,050 m rolls, 10/20 cm spacing), operating since April 2014 (~5,000 rolls).
implication: Local tape extruders exist → they need start connectors, couplings, end plugs: these are the B2B buyers.

summary: Kompass irrigation listings in Algeria are mostly distributors of PE tubes/rubber hoses (Irrinet Boufarik, Irriplast Bordj Menaïel, AITECH, Tupol) with few declared fitting makers (Anabib, Medi Goutte, SIFAT hoses).
implication: Channel = distributors in Mitidja/Sétif/Boumerdès; private-label fittings is the entry model.

summary: SIPSA-Filaha 2026: 850 exhibitors from 40 countries, ~250 international brands, >40,000 visitors expected; mechanisation and agri-tech themes.
implication: Next edition (May 2027) is the main place to meet irrigation buyers.

summary: AGM started producing the first Algerian-developed centre pivot.
implication: Local pivot makers need nozzle bodies, cable clips, caps.

summary: Batimatec 2026 (3–7 May, Algiers) with exhibitors from ~15 countries and 40 start-ups.
implication: Exhibitor catalogue = joinery/construction target list; next edition ~May 2027.

summary: Local furniture gaining vs imports judged less robust, but sector handicapped by manual work and old machinery.
implication: Furniture SMEs grow but are low-tech: they buy small plastic hardware off the shelf (glides, caps) – distributor channel matters.

summary: Divindus AMM (Bab Ezzouar) does series furniture for administrations, local authorities and educational institutions.
implication: Tender-driven volumes of chair tips, glides, end caps; good repeat B2B.

summary: MAM (Manufacture Algérienne du Meuble) is Blum's representative in Algeria.
implication: Premium hinges/runners are imported via reps; local maker can supply complementary plastic parts.

summary: Algeria imported 850 MW of Chinese panels in H1 2025.
implication: Module plastics (junction boxes, corner protectors) arrive embedded in imports; local module makers are few and small.

summary: ENICAB ~20,000 t/yr copper cable; 2,000 t/yr rail cable; export plans.
implication: Cable makers need end caps/reel parts – low complexity.

summary: Cevital partners with a Brazilian group to make electric motors in Algeria (headline).
implication: Future buyer of fan covers/terminal boxes.

summary: No Algerian source found for local thread-protector supply or shortages; searches returned only patents.
implication: Oil & gas protector demand remains unverified – INVESTIGATE via pipe mills.

summary: Searches for 'pièces de rechange plastique introuvable', MOQ or customs pain on Ouedkniss/Facebook returned no Algerian results; pages unreachable.
implication: Pain signals must be collected by phone/visit interviews.
